The jurisdiction's statute is a pure notice act, since it voids unrecorded conveyances only against persons "having actual notice" of the prior deed. The farmer had actual notice of the rancher-to-son deed, so he took subject to it. The buyer paid value, had no actual notice, and recorded, so he takes free of the son's unrecorded deed.
